title: XD-TAU v1.5 expanded physical closure verification

thermoelasticity.domain_and_data: J>0,theta>0,rho0,cv,k,mu,lambda,theta0>0; smooth reference solid; prescribe chi0,chi_t0,theta_init and compatible mechanical/thermal boundary data. Clamped chi=X and theta=theta0 give a reference BC. Pressure traction is P*N=-p_b*J*F^-T*N.
thermoelasticity.theorem_scope: Thermodynamic identities and positive conductivity are exact within the stated domain. The W_FF rank-one tangent is positive at reference equilibrium and locally nearby. A classical local PDE theorem needs regularity, compatibility and strong ellipticity near equilibrium; these finite constitutive checks do not prove global nonlinear thermoelastic existence.

positivity_proof: B_jf=(alpha_f+w_f)*Uj-F_n(Uj) has density b*rho, b=alpha+w-v_n>=c>0, and internal energy b*rho*e-p^2/(2*rho*b)>0 for gamma>1.
Admissible Euler states form a convex cone. Vnew>0 and s_i>=0 prove stage positivity, without clipping. Opposite shared fluxes conserve all three amounts; exact swept displacements give GCL.
moving_mesh_ALE.scope: This is a moving 1-D periodic Euler profile with proved algebraic step domain and measured roundoff. It does not establish full coupled 3-D ALE/FSI convergence or arbitrary-step positivity. The verification assertions do not change the evolution map.

interface_motion.shell_level_set: Phi_o=|x|-Ro(t), Phi_o,t+Ro_dot*|Grad(Phi_o)|=0 at outer regular surface; inner radius fixed
interface_motion.scope: Rigid-motion velocity is globally Lipschitz and its flow a global diffeomorphism, so this advection problem is fully specified. The separate shell formula describes surface accretion and does not silently reinterpret growth as mass-preserving bulk deformation.

shell_modal_stability.equation: M*q_tt+C*q_t+(K0-p*G)*q=f; modal variables are physical displacements
shell_modal_stability.coefficient_units: M kg; C kg/s; K0 N/m; p Pa; G m; q m
shell_modal_stability.energy_proof: For fixed p with K0-pG positive definite, H=0.5*q_t^T*M*q_t+0.5*q^T*(K0-pG)*q is positive definite and Hdot=-q_t^T*C*q_t+q_t^T*f. This proves finite-model Lyapunov stability; C>0 gives asymptotic stability.
shell_modal_stability.pressure_domain: p<pcrit for the positive-pressure reference; pcrit=min_j K0_jj/G_jj=12 Pa here
shell_modal_stability.scope: The matrices define a finite shell-mode model and its exact threshold. They are prescribed calibration data, not a derived buckling threshold for every real shell, geometry, material or load.

inhomogeneous_ADM_initial_data.manifold: flat reference T^3 with each period 2*pi
inhomogeneous_ADM_initial_data.free_data: Atilde=diag(s,-s,0), constant trace-free divergence-free; phi0=Aphi*sin(x); Pi0=0; scalar V=0
inhomogeneous_ADM_initial_data.constructed_data: h_ij=psi^4*delta_ij; K_ij=psi^-2*Atilde_ij+(kappa/3)*h_ij; N0=1,beta0=0 with harmonic time derivatives
inhomogeneous_ADM_initial_data.existence_proof: a=|Atilde|^2/8>0,c=kappa^2/12>0. Small positive constants are subsolutions and large constants supersolutions. Elliptic monotone iteration gives a positive smooth periodic solution.
inhomogeneous_ADM_initial_data.uniqueness_proof: For u=ln psi the nonlinearity a*exp(-8u)+b(x)-c*exp(4u) is strictly decreasing. A positive maximum of the difference of two u solutions contradicts the maximum principle, since their gradients agree there.
inhomogeneous_ADM_initial_data.constraint_derivation: R(h)=-8*psi^-5*Delta psi; |K|^2=psi^-12*|Atilde|^2+kappa^2/3; rho=0.5*psi^-4*|Grad phi0|^2. Hamiltonian residual=-8*psi^-5*elliptic residual. The momentum constraint vanishes by constant TT Atilde, constant kappa and Pi0=0.
inhomogeneous_ADM_initial_data.numerical_method: periodic centered second difference in x; ten unconditional Newton iterations from constant psi0=(a/c)^(1/12), no clipping or line search
inhomogeneous_ADM_initial_data.scope: The analytic argument concerns the continuum initial constraints. Reported Newton residuals are for the discrete elliptic equation and are not exact continuum solutions. A unique local Einstein-scalar development follows from the separately specified harmonic Cauchy theorem; no universal future global theorem is asserted.

references.title: Jiang and Racke, Evolution Equations in Thermoelasticity
Crandall, Ishii and Lions, User's Guide
Friedrich and Rendall, Cauchy Problem for Einstein Equations

proof_vs_computation: Analytic identities/theorem domains are printed separately from finite-difference, Newton and integration measurements. No finite set of passing examples establishes convergence or global regularity of arbitrary PDE couplings.
